What is underneath

A separate 2021 car, not a 2023 repaint.

  • Distinct flat stepped floor, diagonal floor edge, multi-vane bargeboards, narrower squared rear wing and open-spoke 13-inch rims. The 2023 cars retain their ground-effect floor treatment and larger 18-inch wheel covers. Modern tyre dimensions and wheel centres feed both the renderer and the four-patch contact model.
  • Team-specific nose/pod/engine-cover proportion adjustments are shared between browser and native clients. Paint finish distinguishes matte Red Bull/Ferrari from more reflective metallic liveries. Unmirrored alpha-backed sponsor decals follow the curved body rather than stretching one label over the whole car.
  • The 2021 handling preset uses a 752 kg base mass and eight forward ratios. Values beyond regulatory/reference dimensions remain gameplay estimates, not measured chassis telemetry.
  • Shared Rust handling now applies a combined-slip longitudinal/lateral tyre-force budget across all eras, sublinear tyre load sensitivity under downforce, braking/acceleration rear-load transfer and wheelbase-derived steering response. The existing deterministic collision and four-tyre contact solver remain; adding Rapier would not itself supply an F1 tyre model.

Regulatory anchor: FIA 2021 Technical Regulations, issue 8, article 4.1. This is not a full rigid-body suspension, thermal tyre, ERS or DRS simulation.
